# The IssueFilter composition, one row per family, transcribed from
# `linear-search-flow.sh:128-155`.
#
# A silently dropped family yields a valid filter over the WRONG issue set — a
# silent-wrong-answer failure rather than a crash — so the test that reads this
# file carries a row-coverage guard.
#
# The expected column is canonical JSON: serde_json emits object keys sorted,
# which is why `team` appears after `state` in the composed rows even though the
# oracle merges it first. Order is not part of the contract; the fields are.
#
# Spec grammar, semicolon separated: team=, state=, assignee=, label=, text=.
# The injected resolver maps `In Progress` -> state-uuid and nothing else.
#
# Columns: case <TAB> spec <TAB> expected filter
empty		{}
team	team=T1	{"team":{"id":{"eq":"T1"}}}
state	state=In Progress	{"state":{"id":{"eq":"state-uuid"}}}
assignee	assignee=alice	{"assignee":{"name":{"eqIgnoreCase":"alice"}}}
label	label=infra	{"labels":{"name":{"eq":"infra"}}}
text	text=needle	{"title":{"containsIgnoreCase":"needle"}}
team-and-state	team=T1;state=In Progress	{"state":{"id":{"eq":"state-uuid"}},"team":{"id":{"eq":"T1"}}}
every-family	team=T1;state=In Progress;assignee=alice;label=infra;text=needle	{"assignee":{"name":{"eqIgnoreCase":"alice"}},"labels":{"name":{"eq":"infra"}},"state":{"id":{"eq":"state-uuid"}},"team":{"id":{"eq":"T1"}},"title":{"containsIgnoreCase":"needle"}}
